content:
**The engram adapter heals its own pre-guard duplicate rows (#1061)**

**What**: npm run brain:memory:heal-duplicates (cli.mjs op, engram-only) reads an engram export, groups live rec- rows by topic_key, keeps the lowest observation id and plans the rest; --apply hard-deletes them one id at a time ascending, stops at the first failure with an exact report, re-exports and verifies. Refuses (deletes nothing) on differing copies, more than two live rows, an unknown export shape, or an engram version outside 1.20.x. Never touches .memory/records/.
**Why**: memory 2.0 task 1.2a. memory:audit showed the engram backend at rows 2450 distinct 2447: three pre-guard rows imported twice (ids 3092-3094 duplicate 3089-3091, byte-identical). The path the task text allowed (dualWriteRecords) was deleted in #977.
**Where**: brain/scripts/memory/{lib/engram-heal.mjs,backends/engram.mjs,cli.mjs}, openspec/changes/issue-1061-engram-duplicate-heal/.
**Learned**: on engram 1.20.0 a soft delete stays in engram export with deleted_at set, so the audit keeps counting it; only delete <id> --hard removes it, and delete takes the numeric id with --hard after it. Re-importing the same export does not duplicate (deduped by sync_id); a sync_id-rewritten copy does. The real run is the maintainer's, with before/after audit on #1061.
